examples: Our classroom is on the third floor.
nuance: 교실 is the room where a class is held, while 학교 means the whole school building. Use 에 to go there and 에서 for what you do inside.
mistakes: Using 학교 when you mean one 교실

examples: Today there is too much homework.
I want to finish the homework quickly.
nuance: 숙제 is work a teacher assigns to do at home, and Koreans say 숙제를 하다 to do it. The verb 공부하다 means to study in general, which is broader than 숙제.
mistakes: Saying 숙제 만들다 instead of the natural 숙제 하다

examples: There is a Korean exam tomorrow.
nuance: 시험 is a test or exam, and to take one Koreans say 시험을 보다, not 시험을 하다. Passing is 시험에 붙다 and failing is 시험에 떨어지다.
mistakes: Saying 시험을 하다 instead of 시험을 보다

examples: We are not late to class.
nuance: 수업 means the lesson or class period itself, while 교실 is the room and 과목 is the subject. Koreans say 수업을 듣다 to attend or take a class.
mistakes: Confusing 수업 the lesson with 교실 the room

examples: I write words in the notebook.
nuance: 공책 is a blank notebook for writing, and it is counted with the unit 권 like books. The English loanword 노트 is also common in everyday speech.
mistakes: Counting 공책 with 개 instead of the natural 권

examples: I write my name with a pencil.
nuance: 연필 is a wooden pencil, and the counter 자루 is used for long thin items like pens. A ballpoint pen is 볼펜, which is a different writing tool.
mistakes: Confusing 연필 the pencil with 볼펜 the pen

examples: I erase the writing with an eraser.
My eraser is on the desk.
nuance: 지우개 comes from the verb 지우다, which means to erase, plus a noun ending. Koreans use it to rub out pencil marks, so it pairs with 연필 in class.
mistakes: Confusing the verb 지우다 with the noun 지우개

examples: The teacher writes on the blackboard.
The students look at the blackboard.
There are Korean words on the board.
nuance: 칠판 is the board at the front of a classroom that the teacher writes on. Many modern rooms use a white 화이트보드, but 칠판 still covers boards in general.
mistakes: Saying 칠판을 보다 when you mean read it aloud

examples: I go to my hometown during vacation.
I want to rest fully during vacation.
nuance: 방학 is a school break between terms, like summer or winter vacation. A worker taking time off uses 휴가 instead, so the two words are not the same.
mistakes: Using 방학 for a worker holiday instead of 휴가

examples: The student asks the teacher a question.
If you have a question raise your hand.
I want to ask one question.
nuance: 질문 means a question someone asks, and to ask it Koreans say 질문을 하다. The reply to it is 대답, so the two words form a natural pair.
mistakes: Saying 질문을 물어보다, since 질문하다 already means ask

examples: The student answers in a loud voice.
Please give an answer to the question.
nuance: 대답 is the reply given to a question, and Koreans say 대답을 하다 to answer. It is the natural partner of 질문, the question that comes first.
mistakes: Confusing 대답 the answer with 정답 the correct answer

examples: I look up words in the dictionary.
For unknown words look at the dictionary.
This Korean dictionary is very good.
nuance: 사전 is a dictionary you use to look up word meanings, and Koreans say 사전을 찾다 to look something up. Today many learners use a phone 사전 app instead of a paper one.
mistakes: Confusing 사전 the dictionary with 사진 the photo
